2.34 Conclusion

The resurgence of interest in Archaeology

and Heritage within our State has opened up

significant avenues for the exploration, excavation

and preservation of our rich historical legacy. This

renewed focus presents an extensive scope for

delving into the past, with the objectives of

uncovering, safeguarding, promoting and

celebrating the diverse heritage of Tamil Nadu.

Through these endeavours, the department aims

to contribute not only to the collective well-being

but also to the advancement of knowledge,

ultimately placing the history of Tamil Nadu

amongst the broader global narrative.

1.16 Conclusion

The Department of Art and Culture

continues to grow with a steadfast

commitment to preserving, promoting, and

propagating the rich and diverse artistic and

cultural heritage of Tamil Nadu.

This department continues to strengthen the

state's cultural identity through

comprehensive initiatives such as arts

education, welfare schemes for folk artists,

documentation of traditional art forms,

organization of cultural festivals and the

promotion of Tamil arts at national and

international levels.

The department remains committed to

encouraging students to participate in arts

and cultural events, safeguarding traditional

art forms that are on the verge of extinction,

and ensuring the socio-economic

advancement of artists through various

welfare schemes. The department is firmly

future generations.

This department will continue its

unwavering efforts not only to preserve the

State's unique artistic and cultural heritage,

but also to celebrate, nature and transmit its

glorious artistic traditions to future

generations, thereby ensuring Tamil Nadu’s

rich cultural legacy continues to thrive and

inspire generations to come.

DEPARTMENT OF ARCHAEOLOGY

POLICY NOTE

2026-2027

2. Introduction

The essence of Archaeology is the study of

human past which deepens the understanding of

the world in a more meaningful manner.

The study of human past means the study of

human behavioural and cognitive contexts that

transformed the humanity through time period.

Archaeology is a science which methodically

investigates for obtaining a complete picture of

human behavioural and cognitive systems through

material remains. The term archaeology has been

derived from the Greek word. In Greek archaeos

means ancient and logos means discussion,

reason or science.

45

2.1 Objectives of the Department

The State Department of Archaeology was

established in 1961 to achieve the following

objectives:

I. To identify, conserve and preserve ancient and historical monuments.

II. To conduct systematic archaeological explorations and excavations in historically and archaeologically important sites throughout the State.

164. Tamil Nadu’s rich heritage, vibrant culture,

and diverse landscapes make tourism a vital driver of

economic growth, employment generation, and local

empowerment. Investing in tourism strengthens local

livelihoods, preserves our cultural identity, and

accelerates state wide infrastructure development.

165. To ensure a reliable, long-term financing

mechanism for scaling up tourism infrastructure, this

Government proposes to create a dedicated

Sustainable Tourism Development Fund. A Bill to

establish this statutory fund will be introduced in the

present Assembly session to enable seamless

mobilization of resources, catalyze private

investments, and secure sustained funding for future

tourism initiatives across the State.

166. Under our vision to elevate iconic

landmarks to international standards, the Government

will comprehensively develop Mahabalipuram into a

global tourism destination. To realize this vision, we

are submitting a detailed proposal to the Government

of India under its scheme for iconic destination

development to secure a central grant of Rs.200 crore.

This strategic investment will upgrade world-class

80

Tamil Nadu’s position on the global tourism map.

167. To promote river tourism across

Tamil Nadu, an allocation of Rs.53 crore is being made

to develop key riverfronts across three major rivers:

along the Kaveri River from Hogenakkal to Srirangam,

along the Vaigai River in Madurai, and along the

Thamirabarani River from Papanasam to Tirunelveli.

Additionally, to popularize the rich culinary and artistic

heritage of our state, this Government will implement

a project to highlight local food tourism routes

through dedicated Food and Arts Festivals, supported

by an allocation of Rs.20 crore.

168. Demonstrating our commitment to social

welfare and spiritual tourism, senior citizens will be

enabled to visit their chosen holy pilgrimage sites

comfortable lodging, and quality meals, funded by an

allocation of Rs.20 crore in Tamil Nadu. Furthermore,

to cater to the growing influx of devotees, modern rest

and Velankanni at an estimated cost of Rs.60 crore,

ensuring safe and comfortable accommodation for all

pilgrims

nature-based tourism circuits and destinations,
